evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: h1 'Find the flags you forgot to delete' plus bold lede 'Flagsweep is an open-source CLI for engineers who use feature flags. It lists every flag stuck fully on or off for weeks in LaunchDarkly, Unleash or a config file, with the files and lines that still read it.' next to 'pipx install flagsweep' + 'Copy install command'. As the tech lead I could repeat what it does, for whom, and the next step in one read.
evidence.fit: Every brief fact is used: pipx install, LaunchDarkly/Unleash/config tabs in the install section, docs and GitHub URLs exactly as supplied, MIT, 'No paid plan', 'No company yet'. Replaces-cleanup-day and spreadsheet are shown as concrete artifacts (calendar invite moved Mar/Jun/Sep; spreadsheet with '?' owners whose column C the report answers). It also answers my real doubt as a lead with 400 flags: 'Read the list before you delete' explains a kill switch kept off on purpose (search-kill-switch) will be listed at every cutoff.
evidence.distinctiveness: The signature is a sample report with per-flag 120-day rollout step lines and a shaded cutoff window, plus a struck-through code diff and a drawn calendar invite/spreadsheet. Condensed headline face and red 'listed' tags read as a tool, not a SaaS template. The three-step 'how it decides' row is the one familiar block, though each step has its own small drawing.
evidence.proof: The operable report sits in the first screen at 1440 (y≈420). Clicked 14/30/60/90 d chips: summary went 8 of 9 / 27 lines, 6 of 9 / 22 lines, 4 of 9 / 14 lines, 2 of 9 / 6 lines; command line updated to '--stale-after 90d'; verdicts flipped to 'under 90 d'. I summed rows at 30 d (6+3+4+2+5+2=22) and it matches. The file:line list with the dead branch struck through is one scroll down, consistent with the row (new-checkout-flow, 6 lines in 4 files, since Aug 1). Labelled 'Sample report on an example repo, written for this page.'
evidence.craft: Clean grid and consistent rules at 1440 and 768; chips 44px tall. Defects: rows read '2 lines · 1 files' (payments-retry-backoff, search-kill-switch) at 1440; the report table's text is small grey on light grey at the end of each row.
evidence.mobile: 390: Menu button (80x44) opens a panel with How it decides/Install/Docs/GitHub; Escape closes it; tapping 'How it decides' closes the menu and scrolls to the section. Install box and 'Copied: pipx install flagsweep' status appear right under the tapped button. evidence.honesty: Labels at the point of use: 'Sample report ... written for this page' and 'Command and format are illustrative' above the report (visible at 390 too), 'Report entry · sample', '... · example code', and under each source tab 'Example: option names show the shape; the docs list the real ones.' The kill-switch caveat is stated without undermining the product. 'No company yet' and 'No paid plan' are stated plainly at the end, as the brief allows.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: copy button changes to 'Copied' and writes 'Copied: pipx install flagsweep' to a live status (clipboard verified), with a select-and-press-Ctrl+C fallback in code; cutoff chips use aria-pressed and update summary/command/verdicts; flag tabs (new-checkout-flow/legacy-pdf-invoices) and source tabs (LaunchDarkly/Unleash/Config file) switch panels and support arrow keys; menu opens/closes with Escape and outside click. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific and from the engineer's world: 'a flag stuck on never runs its fallback, a flag stuck off never runs the branch it guards', 'line 26 has not run since Aug 1. Delete the check and the old path, keep line 24.', 'The report above answers column C from the flag's own history.' Button says 'Copy install command'. Marked down for '1 files' grammar error in the report and a few long headings ('A flag is listed when it has served one value for longer than your cutoff').
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: headline, lede, install + copy, and the top of the sample report with cutoff chips, '6 of 9 flags ... 22 lines in the repo still read them' and four flag rows are all in view. 390x844: headline, lede, install, the sample label, chips and the summary in view. evidence.clarity: 1440: h1 'Find the feature flags you should have deleted weeks ago.' and lede 'flagsweep scans your code for feature flags, checks each one's history in LaunchDarkly, Unleash or your config files, and lists the flags stuck on one value for weeks, with every file and line to change.' plus 'pipx install flagsweep' + Copy. Clear what, who (implicitly engineers with flags) and next step.
evidence.fit: Uses all brief facts (pipx, three sources, docs and GitHub URLs, MIT, free/no paid plan) and closes with a facts list and 'flagsweep is new. There's no company behind it yet and no usage numbers to show.' The terminal output directly serves 'engineers should understand what it outputs before they scroll'. Missing for me as a lead with 400 flags: no word on kill switches or long-lived ops flags being listed, which is the first doubt before I'd run it on a branch. Source-specific setup is deferred entirely to docs.
evidence.distinctiveness: Terminal output with yellow-highlighted flag names and right-hand annotation callouts tied to output lines at 1440, plus a history explorer with hatched partial-rollout bars. Below that, 'What happens when you run it' is a stock three numbered columns and 'What it replaces' is two struck-through headings plus a card.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the 'Example run against a storefront repo' terminal is in the first screen and shows exactly what I'd get: flag, ON 82 days, history, 'keep the true branch, then delete the flag:' and four file:line references with code. It is static. The operable part (cutoff slider) is the second screen: dragged 7/45/90/120/30 -> 5/4/2/2/4 of 7 listed, statuses changed (e.g. 'Changed 82 days ago' at 90). Numbers are consistent: terminal's '4 flags ... and 2 more: search-v2-ranking, holiday-banner-2025' matches the explorer's 4 of 7 at 30 days.
evidence.craft: At 1440 the annotations line up precisely with terminal lines; tight, consistent spacing and a coherent ink/yellow palette. At 768 the annotations drop below the terminal as a plain 'How to read it' list, disconnected from the lines they explain; footer and nav text is small.
evidence.mobile: 390: stacks and stays readable, no page overflow, but the terminal (the key artifact) is cut at the right and scrolls sideways inside its box (scrollWidth 505 vs 356): code like 'if (flags.newC...' and 'last 90 days' are clipped. The slider is the only control and its track is 16px tall. At 320 the page overflows by 21px and the lede and Copy button are cut off at the right edge. No menu, just two text links.
evidence.honesty: 'Example run against a storefront repo' labels the terminal at every width and the closing note is candid about no company and no usage numbers. But the command ('$ flagsweep' with no arguments) and the exact output format are presented as the real CLI with no note that they are illustrative; the brief supplies no CLI syntax.
evidence.interaction: Copy button changes to 'Copied' for 1.6 s (clipboard verified, textarea fallback in code), but there is no status text and the label never names the object. Slider works by mouse and keyboard (ArrowRight 30 -> 32 days) with a polite live count. That is the whole interactive surface: the terminal is static and timeline rows are not interactive. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Very tight, specific lines: 'Two hundred rows, an owner column that's mostly blank, last edited by someone who left.', 'Run flagsweep whenever you have half an hour and remove whatever it lists.', 'keep the true branch, then delete the flag'. Button text is the default 'Copy'; step copy in 'What happens when you run it' is plain filler-level ('Scan the code').
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: headline, lede, install, and the terminal with new-checkout-flow's file:line list and the action fully in view: the most direct answer to 'what does it output'. 390x844: headline, lede, install and the top of the terminal in view, but the file:line rows are clipped on the right and the action line is cut ('keep the true branch, then delete the flag:' fits, code doesn't).

problems: At 390 the terminal, the page's main proof, is clipped and needs sideways scrolling inside its box; at 320 the page overflows by 21px and the lede and Copy button are cut off.
No answer to the first doubt before running it on 400 flags: kill switches or intentionally permanent flags will show as 'stuck', and the page never says so.
The only interactive control (cutoff slider) is below the first screen with a 16px track, and the CLI command and output format are shown as real without saying they are illustrative.

reason: As the tech lead, A lets me operate the actual decision (cutoff) in the first screen, shows the dead branch line by line, and preempts my real worry, that it will flag a kill switch, before I run it; it also shows per-source setup and labels its examples as illustrative. As the founder I'd ship A tomorrow after fixing '1 files'. B wins on putting file:line output in the desktop first screen with sharper copy, and if the brief's 'before they scroll' were weighted above everything else on a laptop only, B would be close; its mobile clipping and thinner interaction keep it second.
